newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - London hits another peak, dollar weaker.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - London hits another peak, dollar weaker.

text.p: London stocks surged to yet another peak on Friday, lifted by a strong close on Wall Street and optimism over the new Labour government but the rest of Europe was mixed in quiet trade after the Ascension day holiday.
On currency markets, the dollar fell by two yen in early European dealings after fresh Japanese verbal intervention and escalating fears of a rate rise in Japan pummelled it overnight.

London, Europe's biggest bourse, powered forward by over one percent to 4,629.0 points within an hour of opening, overtaking Thursday's record close of 4,580.4, itself the fifth consecutive closing high.
"We have bids and all sorts of euphoria. Just the sort of thing that happens close to the top of a bull market," said Charterhouse Tilney head of research, Richard Jeffrey.

The market was boosted by New York's overnight rebound to 7,136.62 from Wednesday's 140-point plunge. It was also buoyed by the new government's decision to give the central bank more freedom in setting interest rates.
Bullish investors sought shares particularly in financial and drugs companies, causing some stock shortages, dealers said.
"The market is being led by financials and pharmaceuticals and it will take a shock, probably rate rises both sides of the Atlantic, to bring it down," he said.
Bank shares were squeezed higher, adding to their recent strong trend as bid and merger speculation swirled in the sector, currently undergoing some big flotations.
Alliance & Leicester led the advance, putting on 22-1/2p to 649p.
In Frankfurt, stocks nudged ahead slowly but many investors extended the Ascension Thursday holiday into a long weekend, which lowered volumes appreciably.
"There are positive factors coming from many sides on the German share market at the moment," Bayerische Vereinsbank said in a research document.
Despite a mauling in recent days, the dollar was still seen as having a positive impact on the German share market in the mid-term because of the improved prospects for exporters.
"These currency trends, combined with the appealing levels of economic growth abroad, should help improve the outlook for the export sector," said Vereinsbank.
There were some possible clouds on the horizon. "Given an eight-percent rise in the market since the start of April, a bout of profit taking cannot be ruled out," Commerzbank said.
But Paris shares slipped in and out of profit in early, thin trading reacting to a weaker dollar and an opinion poll giving the centre-right just a thin majority ahead of the May 25/June 1 election.
"It's starting to hot up. At the start everybody thought that the right would win, now there are some doubts," a broker said.
In currencies, the dollar fell further in early Europe after the Japanese verbal intervention and fears of a rate rise in Japan struck overnight.
The U.S. currency tumbled to 121.80 yen from 123.76 in late Europe on Thursday on the bout of jitters.
"It's clear Japanese officials are continuing to try to talk down the dollar...there is scope for further falls against the yen," said Nick Stamenkovic, economist at DKB International.
But the weakening of the dollar in reaction to Japan's recent barrage of yen-positive words may make central bank action unnecessary, analysts said.
"The fact the dollar has weakened following concern by Japanese officials suggests there's no need for them to intervene," said Stamenkovic.
Traders said the dollar was unsettled by an article in the Japanese financial daily Nikkei Kinyu speculating on chances of an official discount rate rise in July.
STOCK PRICES AT 0930 GMT
London's FTSE 100 was up 41.8 points at 4,622.2.
The Paris CAC-40 index down 3.37 points to 2,639.94.
Frankfurt's DAX index was up 6.05 points at 3,558.03
CURRENCIES AT 0930 GMT
The dollar stood at 1.7012 marks compared with 1.7073 late in Europe on Thursday and 121.80 yen versus 123.76.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was at $344.50 in early Europe after closing at $343.90 an ounce in London on Wednesday. Silver was $4.83, down one cent.
